label: Subtraction argument and free recombination against the necessary-being nodes
summary: Owner-directed slice (refs #1784), delivering next tests (a) and (b) of attempt 2a1f8da6: the subtraction argument for metaphysical nihilism and free recombination (Hume's dictum) as its support, assessed against the necessary-being nodes STMT-NECESSARY-CONCRETE-AT (b19ffd92) and STMT-NECESSARY-ROOT-BOX-K (cdf897a8). Analyst formulations on the route's own Profile; Baldwin 1996, Rodriguez-Pereyra 1997/2002, Efird and Stoneham 2005, Lowe 1998/2002, Lewis 1986 and Armstrong 1989 are navigation only, no source claim. Findings. (1) Validity and needed premises. A1 (some accessible world has finitely many concreta), A2 throughout (each concretum existing at an accessible world could fail to exist), A3 throughout (conditional subtraction: a concretum that could fail could fail with no newcomer, at one world), transitivity of the route frame (9a6ce384) and excluded middle give 'possibly no concrete object' (result subtraction, induction on the finite list). A1, A2, A3 and transitivity are each needed: omission models keep the others and falsify the conclusion (infinite tail; theist model; pair model; three-world chain); a nonvacuity model satisfies all. The need for excluded middle is not model-tested. The literal A3 ('the non-existence of x does not necessitate the existence of another concretum') is exactly A2 plus the conditional A3 (law 3), so the literal wording already contains A2. (2) Relation to the nodes. The conclusion contradicts the stage-one and box K nodes at their world with no frame condition (laws 1-2). But in the theist model on an S5 frame (God at both worlds, one creature at one world) the box K, S5 and stage-one nodes hold together with A1, A3 throughout, transitivity, free absence for candidates that could be absent and companions; only A2 fails, and only at the necessary being. The box K node excludes A2 at its world (checked incompatibility 6b12525b, node as premise; the weaker stage-one node does too, law 8, but links NECESSARY_11 beside NECESSARY_2, so it is not used as an argument premise), and with excluded middle A2 at w is exactly the denial of the stage-one node (law 8). So the argument reaches the de re nodes only through A2 applied to the candidate necessary being; used against them it adds no premise beyond the node's denial. Its A1/A3 machinery (from individual contingency to joint absence) bears on the de dicto thesis 'necessarily some concretum exists', not on the de re nodes. (3) Recombination. Pairwise free absence among distinct concreta with companions gives A2 at w (result). It does not give A3: in the pair model it holds with A1, A2 and transitivity while A3 and the conclusion fail; the subtraction argument needs a joint principle between pairwise and full recombination. Full recombination over all candidates (the Tractarian ElementaryExistenceAt) gives the conclusion directly (law 4); the box K node already excludes it (065a9092). Restricted to candidates that could be absent, free absence holds in the theist model together with the nodes; the unrestricted form fails there (strict strength order). Certified difference: unrestricted free absence is exactly the restricted form plus the possible absence of every companioned concrete candidate; with companions that difference denies any necessary concretum. Recombination therefore frees the existence of all candidates only in its unrestricted form, and that form's extra content over the restricted form is the contested proposition. The cases that motivate it (separability of ordinary objects in experience and imagination) concern candidates both sides take to be contingent; on them the two forms agree, so they do not discriminate between the forms. (4) Replies, related to existing nodes rather than re-registered. Lowe (analyst formulation): a necessary abstractum whose existence requires some concretum at every accessible world excludes the conclusion (law 6), and with A1, A2 throughout, transitivity and excluded middle it excludes A3 throughout (law 7): Lowe denies subtraction, not contingency. It is compatible with every concretum being contingent and gives no necessary concrete individual (pair model), so it supports neither de re node; its own premises (a necessary abstractum; dependence of every abstractum on concreta, contested for pure sets in the literature, navigation) are not assessed. The route's reply is to deny A2 at the necessary being; that denial is a consequence of the route's independent arguments for the nodes (four arguments conclude the box K node; the stage-one node has several, e.g. inert emptiness 58ff8235), whose premises stay open. Substantive-objection standard, applied to both sides. Target: A2 at the candidate necessary being, equivalently the NECESSARY_2 clause of b19ffd92 and cdf897a8. Mechanism: possible absence of each concretum, then subtraction to a world with none. Independent justification: (i) recombination is not independent at the decisive instance (certified difference above); (ii) conceivability of each being's non-existence with a conceivability-to-possibility bridge (the existing #248 laws 9bbd9b83: the bridge with a conceived not-H yields possibly not-H, which conflicts with box H) is the only candidate independent support, and it is not assessed at this node here. Conclusion: from the subtraction argument and recombination, no substantive objection to the de re nodes beyond A2 itself has been identified; no attacks or alternative_to relation is recorded. Symmetrically, the route gains nothing here: its denial of A2 is only as good as its arguments for the nodes. Rejected: recording 'possibly no concrete object' as an alternative_to or attack on the nodes with evidential weight (fails criterion 3 at the decisive instance); treating the literal A3 as free of A2 (law 3); claiming pairwise recombination supports A3 (pair model); reading Lowe's reply as support for a de re node (pair model). Provisional judgment. The disagreement bottoms out at whether some candidate concrete being exists at every accessible world, that is at A2 for the necessary being, which is the node's denial. Neither side's derivation begs the question: subtraction is valid, and its A1 and A3 are acceptable to the route. Recombination offered as the support for A2 begs the question at the decisive instance, because its unrestricted scope is the restricted principle plus the denial of a necessary concretum. The comparison leaves the nodes' standing where their own arguments put it and does not establish them. Revision conditions: (a) a defended conceivability-to-possibility bridge that applies to a candidate necessary being would give independent support for A2 there and make the subtraction argument a substantive objection; (b) a recombination principle whose warrant covers distinct existences regardless of modal status on independent grounds (for example a combinatorial theory of modality defended without assuming that every concretum is contingent) would do the same; (c) failure of the route's arguments for the nodes would leave A2 at the necessary being uncontested but still unsupported; (d) an argument that a necessary concrete being is incoherent would make A2 analytic.
blocker: A2 at the candidate necessary being is the open crux, not decided by the formal results. Next tests: (1) the conceivability route at this node: instantiate the #248 StrongBridge laws with the route's existence valuation and compare the bridge with the reply that conceiving a being's non-existence shows ignorance of its essence, not possibility (Aquinas ST I q.2 a.1, navigation); (2) a joint subtraction restricted to contingent concreta concluding 'possibly only necessary concreta exist', and its relation to the inert-emptiness premises of 58ff8235; (3) Lowe's dependence premise against pure sets. The need for excluded middle in the subtraction argument is not model-tested.
